title: Runtime material, tensors and zero-copy boundaries
summary: Persistent material meaning is separate from transient runtime placement. ForeignBuffer, Python proxies and ForeignTensor handles are process-local capabilities and are never canonical evidence.
invariants: ForeignBuffer to Python memoryview to NumPy frombuffer is a qualified host-memory zero-copy boundary.
Python-produced processing outputs may remain resident ForeignTensor objects for efficient local chaining.
Materialization to bytes is an explicit boundary operation.
Do not claim an entire pipeline is zero-copy when decode or provider transitions contain explicit copies.

provenance.claim: Persistent ML material meaning separated from transient runtime binding.
